    <ns0:id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12913v2</ns0:id>
    <ns0:title>Quantum Federated Learning for Distributed Quantum Networks</ns0:title>
    <ns0:updated>2024-04-26T13:37:44Z</ns0:updated>
    <ns0:link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12913v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html" />
    <ns0:link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.12913v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf" />
    <ns0:summary>Federated learning is a framework that can learn from distributed networks. It attempts to build a global model based on virtual fusion data without sharing the actual data. Nevertheless, the traditional federated learning process encounters two main challenges: high computational cost and message transmission security. To address these challenges, we propose a quantum federated learning for distributed quantum networks by utilizing interesting characteristics of quantum mechanics. First, we give two methods to extract the data information to the quantum state. It can cope with different acquisition frequencies of data information. Next, a quantum gradient descent algorithm is provided to help clients in the distributed quantum networks to train local models. In other words, the algorithm gives the clients a mechanism to estimate the gradient of the local model in parallel. Compared with the classical counterpart, the proposed algorithm achieves exponential acceleration in dataset scale and quadratic speedup in data dimensionality. And, a quantum secure multi-party computation protocol is designed, which utilizes the Chinese residual theorem. It could avoid errors and overflow problems that may occur in the process of large number operation. Security analysis shows that this quantum protocol can resist common external and internal attacks. Finally, to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we use it to the train federated linear regression model and execute essential computation steps on the Qiskit quantum computing framework.</ns0:summary>

<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"><ns0:entry xmlns:ns0="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:ns1="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom">
    <ns0:id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12913v1</ns0:id>
    <ns0:title>Quantum federated learning based on gradient descent</ns0:title>
    <ns0:updated>2022-12-25T14:37:23Z</ns0:updated>
    <ns0:link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12913v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html" />
    <ns0:link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.12913v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf" />
    <ns0:summary>Federated learning is a distributed learning framework in machine learning, and has been widely studied recently. Generally speaking, there are two main challenges, high computational cost and the security of the transmitted message, in the federated learning process. To address these challenges, we utilize some intriguing characteristics of quantum mechanics to propose a framework for quantum federated learning based on gradient descent. In the proposed framework, it consists of two components. One is a quantum gradient descent algorithm, which has been demonstrated that it can achieve exponential acceleration in dataset scale and quadratic speedup in data dimensionality over the classical counterpart. Namely, the client can fast-train gradients on a quantum platform. The other is a quantum secure multi-party computation protocol that aims to calculate federated gradients safely. The security analysis is shown that this quantum protocol can resist some common external and internal attacks. That is, the local gradient can be aggregated securely. Finally, to illustrated the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we apply it to train federated linear regression models and successfully implement some key computation steps on the Qiskit quantum computing framework.</ns0:summary>
